newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Foreigners' activity on Tel Aviv bourse declines.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners' activity on Tel Aviv bourse declines.

text.p: Financial investment by foreigners in Israel in the first eight months of 1996 grew by 7.3 percent or $1.3 billion to total $19.5 billion, the Bank of Israel said on Tuesday.
Two thirds of the increase was in Israeli shares traded in Tel Aviv and abroad while one third was in foreign currency accounts held by foreigners in Israeli banks.
Most of the increased investment in Israeli shares was in shares traded abroad, mainly because of the numerous share offerings aborad, which totalled $670 million.
Total turnover of shares traded by foreigners on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange was $2.2 billion in this period against $2.5 billion a year earlier.

During this period the total trading volume on the stock market increased by 25 percent so the share of foreigners in total volume dropped to four percent against six percent in the first eight months of last year.

Foreign currency accounts held by foreigners totalled $13.718 billion at the end of August, an increase of $440 million from the end of 1995. Most of the increase was the result of interest accrued on these accounts.

The amount of shekel denominated financial instruments held by foreigners was minimal and accounted for only 1.8 percent of their Israeli portfolio. Shekel deposits held by foreigners at the end of August totalled $99 million while their holdings in Makams amounted to $38 million.
Makams, issued by the Bank of Israel, are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year.
